## Factorise by grouping

Group the four terms into pairs. Factorise each pair, then take out the bracket they share.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$ax+3a+2x+6$

::: {.fragment}

[Group the first two and last two terms.]{.annotation}

$=(ax+3a)+(2x+6)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Take out $a$ and $2$.]{.annotation}

$=a(x+3)+2(x+3)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Take out the shared bracket $x+3$.]{.annotation}

$=(a+2)(x+3)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$ax+3a-2x-6$

Which factor will give you $x+3$ in the second pair? Factorise on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

The second pair is $-2(x+3)$.

$ax+3a-2x-6$

$=a(x+3)-2(x+3)$

$=(a-2)(x+3)$

:::

:::::
